## How long to keep records

Records supporting a claim in a tax return must generally be kept for 5 years
from the date the return is lodged. If a record relates to an asset that may be
subject to capital gains tax, it may need to be kept for longer.

## Written evidence

Written evidence is needed for work-related expense claims. Where total
work-related expenses are more than $300, written evidence must be kept for the
whole amount, not just the amount over $300.

## Form of records

Records may be kept electronically or on paper, provided they are a true and
clear reproduction of the original and show the supplier, the amount, the nature
of the goods or services and the date.
